newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech rail unions say strike starts at midnight.
newsitem.headline: Czech rail unions say strike starts at midnight.

text.p: The main Czech railway unions said on Monday that they would begin a nationwide strike at midnight over safety concerns and overall development of the country's rail system.
"We certainly will strike from midnight," Zdenek Jilek, executive secretary of the Association of Unions of Rail Workers (OSZ), told Reuters.

The planned 48-hour strike to support demands for a long-term plan to save the failing rail system, is expected to completely shut passenger and freight traffic on domestic and international lines throughout the Czech Republic.

The OSZ said that if it did not get "sufficient" guarantees of solutions to the "massive problems" relating to the quality and development of the state railways, Ceske Drahy s.p., it would prolong the strike.
The strike would also be repeated every 24 hours, it said in a statement.

Union leaders said that the action carried no demands for pay increases, but was meant to clean up "massive problems" in the leadership of Ceske Drahy and the transport policy of the Czech government.
The OSZ represents all Czech railway workers, which total more than 100,000 employees, excluding train drivers who have yet to say whether they would support the strike.
It's not expected that any trains could run even if the drivers did not strike with their colleagues.
Czech Transport Minister Martin Riman has called a news conference for today to discuss the government's position.
Losses of Ceske Drahy, one of the few large companies not yet privatised by the post-Communist government, have been mounting.

The Czech news agency CTK quoted officials of Ceske Drahy on Monday as saying that the company expected to post losses of about seven billion crowns in 1997 after a six billion crown loss last year, and four billion the year before.
